section.sectionSummaryBrief: Explains the Midrashic question on the verse "Kedoshim Tihyu" and the resolution in Likkutei Torah.
section.t: "Speak to the entire assembly of the children of Israel, etc., 'You shall be holy, for I am holy.'"1
And it is brought in the Midrash:2
"One might think [you could be] like Me,
therefore the verse teaches 'for I am holy'—
My holiness is above your holiness."
And it needs to be understood:3
How is it even possible to have a mere supposition that they could be like Me?
And superficially, one could say,
that the reason for the supposition "one might think [you could be] like Me"
(even though a created being is incomparable to the Creator)
is,
because from the wording of the verse "You shall be holy, for I am holy"
(where "for I am holy" is the reason and explanation for "You shall be holy")
it implies,
that the command "You shall be holy" means that the holiness of Israel must be similar to His holiness—"one might think [you could be] like Me."
[And one could explain this,
since Israel and the Holy One, blessed be He, are entirely one,4
therefore Israel are connected to all matters that are above.]
But based on this, it needs to be understood
(on the other hand)
[regarding] the conclusion of the Midrash, "My holiness is above your holiness"—
how does this align with the wording of the verse "for I am holy"?
And it is explained in Likkutei Torah:5
that "your holiness" is the holiness drawn down through an arousal from below
(the performance of the mitzvot),
and "My holiness that is above your holiness" is a most elevated holiness that no arousal from below
(of the performance of the mitzvot)
reaches there,
and it is drawn down through teshuvah.
And explanation is needed:
After all, teshuvah is also the service of man,
an arousal from below,
so why is it called "My holiness that is above your holiness"?
